target_schema.name: global_clinical
target_schema.title: Unified Global Clinical Data Schema (Synthea + OMOP CDM)

fields.name: value_type
fields.description: Datatype of the recorded value (text or numeric).

fields.name: immunization_id
fields.description: Surrogate key introduced for target table mechanics; no source counterpart.

fields.name: allergy_id
fields.description: Surrogate key introduced for target table mechanics; no source counterpart.

conflicts.description: The same real-world entity (an individual receiving care) is named 'patients' in Synthea and 'person' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single target resource 'patient'; the identification attribute is normalized to 'patient_id'.

conflicts.description: Synthea calls the care-contact event 'encounters', while OMOP names it 'visit_occurrence' and additionally introduces a nested 'visit_detail'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target 'encounter' with encounter_id; the OMOP visit_detail level is treated as a structural sub-detail conflict (see Structure).

conflicts.description: Synthea table 'conditions' corresponds to OMOP 'condition_occurrence'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target 'condition_occurrence'.

conflicts.description: Synthea 'medications' corresponds to OMOP 'drug_exposure'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target 'drug_exposure'.

conflicts.description: Synthea 'procedures' corresponds to OMOP 'procedure_occurrence'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target 'procedure_occurrence'.

conflicts.description: Synthea 'organizations' corresponds to OMOP 'care_site'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target 'organization' with organization_id.

conflicts.description: Misspelled column name 'speciality' in Synthea versus correctly spelled 'specialty' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized spelling to 'specialty_source_value' / 'specialty_concept_id'.

conflicts.description: Synthea imaging_studies uses column names containing spaces and non-snake_case naming.
conflicts.resolution: All column names converted to snake_case (e.g. 'body site code' -> body_site_code; 'date' -> study_date to avoid a reserved/generic name).

conflicts.description: Homonym conflict: the Synthea 'provider' column in encounters is documented as a foreign key to the organization, not to a clinician, clashing with the general meaning of 'provider'.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped to care_site_id referencing the organization entity; clinician-level reference retained separately as provider_id from OMOP.

conflicts.description: Synthea 'observations' overlaps both OMOP 'observation' and OMOP 'measurement', which are distinct named entities.
conflicts.resolution: Synthea observations merged into target 'observation'; OMOP 'measurement' retained as its own target resource to preserve key distinctness (see Structure/Key).

conflicts.description: Synthea monetary cost fields are typed as string but represent numeric monetary amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to number in the target (base_cost, cost).

conflicts.description: OMOP birth component fields are declared as 'date' but semantically hold integer calendar components.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to integer; full birth moment consolidated into birth_date.

conflicts.description: Geographic coordinates declared as string but are numeric quantities.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to number.

conflicts.description: vocabulary_name is declared as integer but holds descriptive text.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to string.

conflicts.description: Identifier column declared as 'date' although it is a surrogate identifier.
conflicts.resolution: Treated as string identifier (out of unified core; flagged for correction).

conflicts.description: The invalid_reason code attribute is declared as 'date' in several OMOP tables but holds alphabetic codes (D/U).
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to string in the target concept resource.

conflicts.description: Synthea describes encounter start/stop as date-and-time but types them as 'date'; OMOP supplies separate date and datetime columns.
conflicts.resolution: Split into start_date/end_date (date) and start_datetime/end_datetime (datetime) in the target encounter.

conflicts.description: term_modifiers declared as integer but semantically carries concatenated textual modifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to string (out of unified core; flagged for correction).

conflicts.description: Concept identifier columns are inconsistently typed as integer or number across OMOP tables vs string elsewhere.
conflicts.resolution: All concept identifiers standardized to string.

conflicts.description: Synthea encodes gender as single letters (m/f); OMOP uses vocabulary concept identifiers plus a verbatim source value.
conflicts.resolution: Both representations retained: gender_source_value holds Synthea's letter and OMOP's source value, gender_concept_id holds the OMOP standard concept.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores race/ethnicity as free-text descriptions, whereas OMOP uses coded concept identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Separated into *_source_value (verbatim text) and *_concept_id (standardized code) columns.

conflicts.description: Synthea keeps clinical codes inline using domain-specific vocabularies (SNOMED-CT, RxNorm, LOINC, CVX, DICOM); OMOP centralizes codes in the CONCEPT vocabulary with concept identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Source codes preserved as *_source_value; standardized mapping retained through *_concept_id referencing the shared concept resource.

conflicts.description: Units of measure are free text in Synthea but coded concepts in OMOP; representational scale differs.
conflicts.resolution: unit_source_value preserves the verbatim unit and unit_concept_id preserves the coded unit; both retained.

conflicts.description: Synthea's single base 'cost' field conflates several semantically distinct monetary measures that OMOP separates (charge, incurred cost, amounts paid).
conflicts.resolution: Synthea encounters.cost mapped to base_cost; distinct OMOP monetary semantics kept separate rather than merged.

conflicts.description: Encounter class is an enumerated string in Synthea (ambulatory, emergency...) while OMOP uses a visit concept identifier.
conflicts.resolution: encounter_class preserves the Synthea category string; encounter_concept_id preserves the OMOP coded visit type.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses compact single-letter codes (m/s for marital status) whose semantics are non-obvious.
conflicts.resolution: Values retained verbatim in marital_status; categorical encoding documented as a semantic resolution concern.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds address attributes (street/city/state/zip) directly in each entity; OMOP normalizes them into a separate LOCATION resource referenced by foreign key.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into a reusable target 'location' resource with location_id foreign keys from patient/organization; Synthea inline address columns retained on patient/organization for lossless capture.

conflicts.description: OMOP fully normalizes a terminology/vocabulary subsystem; Synthea keeps inline codes with no such reference layer.
conflicts.resolution: Core 'concept' resource retained as the shared coding reference; deeper vocabulary tables treated as an OMOP-only subsystem to be materialized alongside.

conflicts.description: Synthea collapses all observation results into a single typed-union value column plus a value_type marker; OMOP splits results across value_as_number/value_as_string/value_as_concept_id.
conflicts.resolution: Value disaggregated into value_as_number, value_as_string and value_as_concept_id; Synthea value_type preserved as a discriminator column.

conflicts.description: OMOP decomposes a visit into a parent visit_occurrence and a nested visit_detail, whereas Synthea has a single flat encounter level.
conflicts.resolution: Flat 'encounter' resource retained as the unified parent; visit_detail_id columns preserved on event tables for OMOP lineage.

conflicts.description: Synthea models death as an attribute (deathdate) on the patient, while OMOP models it as a separate DEATH resource with cause and type.
conflicts.resolution: Death retained as a dedicated target 'death' resource keyed by patient_id; the plain death_date is also projected onto the patient for the Synthea view.

conflicts.description: Synthea holds line-item costs inline on each event; OMOP normalizes all costs into a polymorphic COST resource.
conflicts.resolution: Synthea inline costs retained on each event (base_cost/cost); the normalized OMOP COST resource is recognized as a separate structural representation of the same measures.

conflicts.description: Both schemas model one patient to many encounters/events, but this 1:N relationship is only implicitly expressed in Synthea via foreign-key columns.
conflicts.resolution: 1:N preserved with patient_id foreign keys on all event resources.

conflicts.description: Provider-to-organization membership is 1:N from organization to provider in both schemas, but Synthea expresses it as a plain FK column without a declared relationship.
conflicts.resolution: care_site_id foreign key on provider referencing organization.

conflicts.description: OMOP contains self-referential and bridge tables expressing many-to-many hierarchies (concept ancestry, concept/relationship, episode-event), with no Synthea counterpart.
conflicts.resolution: Recognized as OMOP-only N:M structures; retained as separate bridge resources outside the merged core entities.

conflicts.description: OMOP imposes a strict 1:N parent-child cardinality between visit_occurrence and visit_detail; Synthea has no equivalent nesting level.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as encounter (parent) to nested visit_detail children via visit_detail_id on event tables.

conflicts.description: OMOP links person and care_site to a shared location (reused N:1), while Synthea stores a distinct inline address per row with no sharing.
conflicts.resolution: Location normalized to a shared 1:N reference so multiple entities can point to one location_id.

conflicts.description: Synthea child tables declare no primary key at all, whereas their OMOP counterparts expose explicit surrogate identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Target primary keys drawn from the OMOP identifiers where available; purely synthetic surrogate keys (immunization_id, allergy_id) introduced where no source key exists.

conflicts.description: Primary key identification conflict: the patient identifier is named 'id' in Synthea and 'person_id' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified primary key patient_id with provenance from both.

conflicts.description: Encounter primary key is named 'id' in Synthea and 'visit_occurrence_id' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified primary key encounter_id with provenance from both.

conflicts.description: Foreign-key identification difference: Synthea references the organization via a column named 'organization', OMOP via 'care_site_id'.
conflicts.resolution: Both mapped to care_site_id referencing the unified organization key.

conflicts.description: OMOP distinguishes standardized concept keys from source concept keys for the same event, in contrast to Synthea's single inline code.
conflicts.resolution: Both standardized (*_concept_id) and source (*_source_concept_id/*_source_value) keys retained, all ultimately referencing the shared concept resource.

conflicts.description: Synthea conflates provider and organization identity naming (encounters.provider points to organization), risking key confusion between the physician entity and the facility entity.
conflicts.resolution: Separated into distinct care_site_id (organization) and provider_id (clinician) keys; the Synthea encounters.provider column definitively mapped to care_site_id.
